# 2 Samuel Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 179v–180r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_011_page_001.jpg, 2SA_011_page_002.jpg

---

**11:1** And-it-was at-[the]-turn of-the-year, at-[the]-time of-[the]-going-out of-the-kings [ha-melakhim], and-sent David Yo'av and-his-servants with-him and-all Yisra'el, and-they-destroyed [the]-sons of-Ammon and-besieged Rabbah. And-David [was]-sitting [yoshev] in-Yerushalayim.

**11:2** And-it-was at-[the]-time of-the-evening, and-rose David from-upon his-bed and-walked-about upon the-roof of-[the]-house of-the-king. And-he-saw a-woman bathing [rochetset] from-upon the-roof, and-the-woman [was]-good of-appearance [tovat mar'eh] exceedingly.

**11:3** And-sent David and-inquired about the-woman. And-[one]-said, "Is-not this Bat-Sheva daughter of-Eli'am, wife of-Uriyah the-Chitti?"

**11:4** And-sent David messengers and-took-her, and-she-came to-him and-he-lay-with-her — and-she [was]-purifying-herself [mitqaddeshet] from-her-uncleanness [tum'atah] — and-she-returned to her-house.

**11:5** And-conceived the-woman, and-she-sent and-told David and-said, "Pregnant [am]-I [harah anokhi]."

**11:6** And-sent David to Yo'av, "Send to-me Uriyah the-Chitti." And-sent Yo'av Uriyah to David.

**11:7** And-came Uriyah to-him, and-asked David for-[the]-welfare [shalom] of-Yo'av and-for-[the]-welfare of-the-people and-for-[the]-welfare of-the-war.

**11:8** And-said David to-Uriyah, "Go-down to-your-house and-wash your-feet." And-went-out Uriyah from-[the]-house of-the-king, and-went-out after-him a-gift [mas'at] of-the-king.

**11:9** And-lay-down Uriyah [at the]-entrance of-[the]-house of-the-king with all [the]-servants of-his-lord, and-did-not go-down to his-house.

**11:10** And-they-told David, saying, "Not went-down Uriyah to his-house." And-said David to Uriyah, "Have-you-not come from-a-journey? Why did-you-not go-down to your-house?"

**11:11** And-said Uriyah to David, "The-ark and-Yisra'el and-Yehudah [are]-dwelling in-booths [sukkot], and-my-lord Yo'av and-[the]-servants of-my-lord upon [the]-face of-the-field [are]-encamped. And-I — shall-I-go to my-house to-eat and-to-drink and-to-lie-with my-wife? By-your-life [chayyekha] and-by-[the]-life of-your-soul [chey nafshekha], I-will-not do this thing!"

**11:12** And-said David to Uriyah, "Stay also today here, and-tomorrow I-will-send-you." And-stayed Uriyah in-Yerushalayim that day and-the-next.

**11:13** And-called-him David, and-he-ate before-him and-drank, and-he-made-him-drunk [vayshakkerehu]. And-he-went-out in-the-evening to-lie-down on-his-bed with [the]-servants of-his-lord, and-to his-house he-did-not go-down.

**11:14** And-it-was in-the-morning, and-wrote David a-letter [sefer] to Yo'av, and-sent [it] by-[the]-hand of-Uriyah.

**11:15** And-he-wrote in-the-letter, saying, "Set [havu] Uriyah in-[the]-face of-the-battle, the-strongest [ha-chazaqah], and-turn-back from-behind-him, and-he-shall-be-struck and-die."

**11:16** And-it-was when-Yo'av kept-watch [shamar] over the-city, and-he-placed Uriyah to the-place where he-knew that men of-strength [anshey-chayil] [were] there.

**11:17** And-went-out [the]-men of-the-city and-fought with Yo'av, and-fell [some] from the-people, from-[the]-servants of-David, and-died also Uriyah the-Chitti.

**11:18** And-sent Yo'av and-told David all [the]-matters of-the-war.

**11:19** And-he-commanded the-messenger, saying, "When-you-finish telling all [the]-matters of-the-war to the-king,

**11:20** and-it-shall-be if the-anger of-the-king rises and-he-says to-you, 'Why did-you-approach so-near to the-city to-fight? Did-you-not know that they-would-shoot from-upon the-wall?

**11:21** Who struck Avimelekh son of-Yerubboshet? Did-not a-woman throw upon-him an-upper-millstone from-upon the-wall and-he-died in-Tevets? Why did-you-approach the-wall?' And-you-shall-say, 'Also your-servant Uriyah the-Chitti is-dead.'"

**11:22** And-went the-messenger, and-came and-told David all that Yo'av had-sent-him [for].

**11:23** And-said the-messenger to David, "For the-men prevailed over-us, and-went-out to-us into-the-field, and-we-were upon-them up-to [the]-entrance of-the-gate.

**11:24** And-shot the-shooters [ha-morim] at your-servants from-upon the-wall, and-died [some] from-[the]-servants of-the-king, and-also your-servant Uriyah the-Chitti is-dead."

**11:25** And-said David to the-messenger, "Thus you-shall-say to Yo'av, 'Do-not let-this-thing be-evil in-your-eyes [al-yera ba-einekha], for thus and-thus the-sword devours [tokhal]. Strengthen [hachzeq] your-battle against the-city and-overthrow-it.' And-encourage-him [chazzqehu]."

**11:26** And-heard [the]-wife of-Uriyah that Uriyah her-husband had-died, and-she-mourned [vatispod] over her-lord [ba'alah].

**11:27** And-passed the-mourning [ha-evel], and-sent David and-gathered-her to his-house, and-she-became to-him as-a-wife, and-she-bore to-him a-son. And-the-thing that David had-done was-evil [vayera] in-[the]-eyes of-YHWH.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — ha-melakhim:** The MT reads "the kings" (*ha-melakhim*). Some manuscripts and the LXX read "the messengers" (*ha-mal'akhim*). The reading "kings" (i.e., the time when kings go out to war) is supported by the Leningrad Codex and makes excellent contextual sense: kings go out — but David stays home.

**v.1 — yoshev:** David "sits" (*yoshev*) in Jerusalem. The same verb used of Mephibosheth "sitting" at the king's table in ch. 9. Here the sitting is not hospitality but abdication of kingly duty.

**v.4 — mitqaddeshet mitum'atah:** This parenthetical clause — "and she was purifying herself from her uncleanness" — is a narrator's note, not part of the action sequence. It establishes that Bathsheba's ritual immersion (following menstruation) is why she was bathing, and simultaneously confirms that any resulting pregnancy must be David's.

**v.11 — chey nafshekha:** Uriah's oath "by your life and by the life of your soul" is deeply ironic. He swears by the life of the king who is plotting his death. The word *nephesh* (soul/life) carries its full weight here.

**v.14-15 — sefer:** David writes a "letter" (*sefer*) — the same word used for "book" or "scroll." Uriah carries his own death warrant. The narrative horror is in the silence: the text does not tell us what Uriah thought as he carried the sealed letter.

**v.21 — Avimelekh son of Yerubboshet:** The MT reads "Yerubboshet" (ירבשת), a theologically corrected form of "Yerubbaal" (Gideon's other name), replacing *baal* with *boshet* ("shame"). The reference is to Judges 9:53.

**v.25 — tokhal ha-cherev:** "The sword devours" (*tokhal*) — the sword is personified as a consumer. David's callous proverb — "the sword devours now this one, now that one" — is the moral nadir of the chapter. He reduces Uriah's murder to a military commonplace.

**v.27 — vayera:** The chapter's final word is devastating: "the thing was evil (*ra*) in the eyes of YHWH." The verb *yera* (was evil) echoes David's command to Joab: "do not let this thing be evil (*yera*) in your eyes" (v.25). What David told Joab to overlook, YHWH does not.

*— EMET*
